name: Tailscale DERP
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Runs derper, Tailscale's relay server, for your tailnet's own DERP map. Use a domain on port 443 for a Let's Encrypt certificate, or an IP address on any port for a self-signed one; STUN needs a second, UDP allocation. Clients can't be verified without tailscaled, so anyone who finds it can relay their encrypted traffic through it.
startup: if [ "{{CERT_MODE}}" = letsencrypt ] && [ "{{SERVER_PORT}}" != 443 ]; then echo "Let's Encrypt certificates need the server on port 443, and this one is on {{SERVER_PORT}}. Give the server port 443, or set Certificate to manual."; exit 1; fi; exec ./derper -c derper.json -a :{{SERVER_PORT}} -http-port -1 -stun-port {{STUN_PORT}} -hostname "{{DERP_HOSTNAME}}" -certmode {{CERT_MODE}} -certdir certs

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Tailscale DERP: builds derper, Tailscale's relay server, from Tailscale's
# source at the chosen release, with the newest Go from go.dev (checked
# against its SHA-256). The key (derper.json) and certificates are never
# touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
ua="raptor-installer (+https://raptorpanel.net)"
# Go and its build cache live in the server's folder while building (the
# install's /tmp is small), removed when the script ends.
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'chmod -R u+w "$work" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "derper can't be built for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

# Tailscale's releases, from Go's module proxy.
want="${VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$want" = latest ]; then
    tag=$(curl -fsSL -A "$ua" https://proxy.golang.org/tailscale.com/@latest | jq -r .Version) ||
        fail "Go's module proxy can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
else
    tag="v${want#v}"
    code=$(curl -sSL -A "$ua" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://proxy.golang.org/tailscale.com/@v/$tag.info") ||
        fail "Go's module proxy can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    [ "$code" = 200 ] || fail "Tailscale has no release $tag. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 1.104.7, then reinstall."
fi

if [ -x derper ] && [ "$(cat .derper-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "derper $tag is already installed."
else
    go=$(curl -fsSL -A "$ua" 'https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json' |
        jq -r --arg a "$arch" '.[0] as $r | $r.files[] | select(.os == "linux" and .arch == $a and .kind == "archive") | "\($r.version) \(.filename) \(.sha256)"') ||
        fail "go.dev can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    read -r gover gofile gosum <<<"$go"
    echo "Downloading $gover to build with."
    curl -fsSL -A "$ua" -o "$work/$gofile" "https://go.dev/dl/$gofile"
    echo "$gosum  $work/$gofile" | sha256sum -c --quiet - || fail "The Go download doesn't match its checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xzf "$work/$gofile" -C "$work"
    rm -f "$work/$gofile"
    echo "Building derper $tag."
    mkdir -p "$work/tmp"
    # Two build jobs, so the build fits in about 1 GiB of memory.
    env -u GOFLAGS PATH="$work/go/bin:$PATH" HOME="$work" GOPATH="$work/gopath" GOCACHE="$work/cache" GOTMPDIR="$work/tmp" \
        GOTOOLCHAIN=auto CGO_ENABLED=0 GOBIN="$work/bin" \
        go install -p 2 -trimpath -ldflags=-s "tailscale.com/cmd/derper@$tag"
    install -m 0755 "$work/bin/derper" derper.new
    mv -f derper.new derper
    echo "$tag" > .derper-version
fi
mkdir -p certs
echo "Installed derper $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Tailscale release derper is built from, such as 1.104.7, or latest.

variables.name: Hostname
variables.description: The domain name that points at this server, or its public IP address.

variables.name: Certificate
variables.description: letsencrypt gets a certificate for the domain (the server must be on port 443); manual uses certs/<hostname>.crt and .key, made for you when the hostname is an IP address.

variables.name: STUN port
variables.description: The UDP port STUN answers on, which helps devices connect directly: one of the server's allocations.
